413016: Anneianum was located in the Etruscan Apennines, along the road from Faventia to Florentia.
413017: City of the Frentani, situated on a hill about 5 miles from the Adriatic Sea, and 8 miles from the mouth of the river Sagrus or Sangro in Italy.
413024: Roman city situated on mineral springs known today as Terme di Cotilia or Terme di Vespasiano in the Sabina region, Italy
413025: Located in Etruria, Aquae Passeris was frequented in antiquity for its thermal springs, as noted by Martial. The site is included on the Tabula Peutingeriana, placing it on the road from Rome to Volsinii. Its location likely corresponds to that of Bacucco, a comune to the north of Viterbo.
413030: Arna was an ancient city of Umbria that was controlled by Etruscans in the fourth century BCE.
413032: Arretium (the Etruscan Aritim) was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae and described by Livy as one of the "Capitae Etruriae". The Romans captured the city in 311 B.C. and it became a station on the via Cassia.
413035: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Asciano
413036: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.
413037: A Roman settlement built atop an earlier Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.
413039: Aternum (modern Pescara) was a settlement at the mouth of the Aternus River.
413041: An ancient settlement of Umbria mentioned only by Pliny the Elder. Numerous inscriptions discovered at the site indicate that Attidium achieved the status of a municipium.
413042: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 *Aufenginum
413043: Aufinum, long thought to have been located at modern Ofena, which reflects the ancient name, has been shown by recent excavations to have been located some 5km further south, near modern Capestrano. Aufinum was an ancient center of the Abruzzo. Pliny lists the Aufinates Cismontani among the communities of the Vestini.
413044: *Aurinia/Saturnia was a settlement in Etruria. Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed it was founded by the Pelasgians. Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.
413045: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.
413046: Aveia was a settlement of the Vestini in the valley of the Aterno River.
413048: Axia was an Etruscan center located to the west of Viterbo.
413051: Badies is a site (vicus) along the Via Salaria mentioned in the Antonine Itinerary. Its location is no longer certain.
413052: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Balneum Regis
413054: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE.
413056: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Caelanum
413058: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Cales
413060: Camerinum was a town in Umbria on the frontiers of Picenum that was allied to Rome from 309 B.C.
413061: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Campovalano
413062: An ancient urban center in Faliscan territory adjacent to Etruria, Capena was sacked by the Romans in 390 BC.
413063: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Capestrano
413065: An ancient settlement originating the late fourth or third centuries BC and lying along the route of the Roman Via Flaminia.
413066: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Casone
413067: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Castellina
413068: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelluccio di Pienza
413069: Castellum Firmanorum was the ancient port of Firmum Picenum.
413070: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelsecco
413071: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C2 Castiglione del Lago
413072: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Castro
413073: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Novum
413074: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Truentinum
413076: Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) was an ancient coastal settlement in Tyrrhenian Etruria. The emperor Trajan rebuilt the harbor at the site in 106/7 and Pliny the Younger mentions its name, Centum Cellae. Saracens destroyed the city in A.D. 812.
413077: Cetamura is an ancient hilltop settlement with occupation phases stretching from the Etruscans to the Romans to the Medieval period. The site is located near Gaiole, Radda and Castellina in Chianti, Italy.
413078: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.
413079: The site of Le Ciliegeta, near the source of the river Arno, served as a rich stips votiva. The site was discovered in 1836. The finds included over 600 bronzes, more than 1,000 pieces of aes rude, 2,000 weapons, and other artifacts.
413082: Cingulum was a town in Picenum.
413084: The Civita di Bagnoregio was originally founded by the Etruscans.
413085: Civita di Bagno is the modern name for a small settlement that dates back at least to the Roman Late Republican period. Within the modern town, several key monuments are known, such as a podium temple (late 2nd c. BCE?), identified as that of Feronia by an inscription from the reign of Tiberius, a bath complex beneath Palazzo Oliva, and the medieval remains of the cathedral of San Massimo which reuses much ancient material, as well as funerary remains along the ancient road network. On the adjacent Moritola hill is a vast system of terracing, which in its earliest phase dates to the 2nd c. BCE, that supported a monumental complex of difficult interpretation, but with an important hydraulic infrastructure. This complex underwent multiple modifications over the centuries; in the 5th c. CE the complex was transformed by the installation of two kilns and a limekiln. By the 6th c. CE Civita di Bagno was the seat of a bishop.
413086: La Cività di Spedino was a fortified upland center (951 m ASL) in the territory of the Aequi.
413087: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Civitalba
413090: A city of the Aequiculi located in the valley of the Salto river.
413093: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.
413096: Clusium, the Etruscan Clevsin (modern Chiusi), was a major city of Etruria. Lars Porsena was a sixth century B.C. king of Clusium.
413097: A city of the Carricini Samnites. Its site was surveyed and partially excavated in the 19th and 20th centuries in the vicinity of modern Piano La Roma, a locality to the northwest of modern Casoli.
413098: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Colle delle Fate
413099: A hilltop villa near Tifernum Tiberinum commonly associated with one of the villas of Pliny the Younger.
413100: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Collepezzuto
413101: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada Altavilla
413102: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada S. Rustico
413103: Corchiano was the site of a wealthy settlement in the Ager Faliscus that was in proximity to the Via Amerina.
413104: The environs of Corciano were inhabited by Etruscans and, later, there is evidence for Roman villas. In 1812, a series of bronze panels from an Etruscan parade chariot was discovered at Castel San Mariano di Corciano.
413105: Corfinium was the principal city of the Paeligni in the valley of the Aternus river. The site becomes the capital of the breakaway Italic groups that oppose Rome during the Social War.
413106: An Umbrian city that, under Etruscan influence, expanded and came to be called 'Curtun'. Later it became the Roman colony of Cortino.
413109: The principal archaeological remains found in the "La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo" site are those of a late Republican sanctuary dating to the third through first centuries B.C.
413112: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.
413113: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Cupra Montana
413114: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city in the Tiber River valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.
413118: Doganella was an important Etruscan settlement of the Albegna valley, occupied between ca. 600 and 400 B.C. The city may have comprised as many as 240 ha.
413121: Eretum was a settlement of the Sabines and is involved in legendary accounts of early Rome.
413124: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.
413125: A fortified town located some 6 km from Falerii Veteres and established by the ancient Romans ca. 241 B.C.
413126: Falerii Veteres was the principal city of the Faliscans. It is located on a tuff outcropping at the point where several tributaries of the Treia join to flow into the Tiber. After rebelling against Rome in 241 B.C., Falerii suffered serious reversals of fortune.
413127: Falerio was the site of a substantial ancient settlement on the left bank of the river Tinna. Under Augustus, a colony of veterans assigned to the tribus Velina was established there.
413129: Fanum Fortunae, the site of a shrine to Fortuna, is first mentioned in the ancient sources in 49 B.C. when Iulius Caesar held the town. An Augustan colony was established at the site and the Romans prevailed in the Battle of Fano in A.D. 271. The town was eventually destroyed by the Ostrogoths.
413132: Ferentium (modern Ferento) was a city of Etruria first mentioned in the Liber Coloniarum ca. 123 BC that became a Roman municipium after the Social War. Substantial remains of the city remain; the site was the birthplace of Otho and is noted for its fine stone monuments and statues.
413133: Fescennium is the ancient name of a Faliscan settlement located ca. 5 km south of Falerii Veteres. The site, which was inhabited from the second millennium to the third century BCE, is often also called by the modern Italian name Narce (derived from an associated peak).
413134: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 *Firmidianum
413135: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.
413138: Florentia (modern Florence / Firenze) was founded as a colony for military veterans ca. 80 B.C. by Lucius Cornelius Sulla.
413140: Originally the site of a shrine dedicated to the river god Clitumnus and later a paleochristian shrine. The temple was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.
413141: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Fontecchio
413142: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.
413143: A settlement in Etruria situated on the Via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Cosa according to the Antonine Itinerary.
413144: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Forum Cassii
413145: An ancient road station on the Via Clodia.
413146: A town of the Sabines mentioned by Pliny the Elder.
413147: Caius Flaminius founded Forum Flaminii in 220 B.C. during the construction of the Via Flaminia.
413148: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The market center seems to have remained active until at least the fourth century and by the fifth century, a bishopric is established there.
413149: An ancient Roman colony, founded in the time of Gaius Sempronius Gracchus.
413151: Fulginiae was an ancient town of Umbria, Italy, on the later line of the Via Flaminia, ca. 20 km south of Nuceria.
413152: A vicus of the Vestini located in the upper Aterno valley in Abruzzo. The ancient settlement was located some 15 km south of modern L'Aquila, in the vicinity of S. Maria di Forfona near Barisciano. Furfo lay on the Via Claudia Nova between Amiternum and Peltuinum.
413154: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Galeata
413156: Ghiaccio Forte was an Etruscan settlement, most likely founded in the fourth century B.C., that was sacked by the Romans ca. 280 B.C.
413157: The port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinia.
413158: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Grotte di Castro
413163: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as a colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests the city may have originated as a late sixth-century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.
413164: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicates previous Etruscan occupation at the site.
413165: A sanctuary in the territory of the Paeligni dedicated to Hercules Curinus situated on an artificial terrace on the slopes of Mount Morrone. The terrace sanctuary looks over Sulmo in the valley below.
413166: An ancient settlement in Picenum at modern Villa Potenza in Marche, Comune di Macerata, Italy.
413167: Helvillum was a vicus in Umbria located about 10 Roman miles from Aesis (Jesi).
413170: Hispellum (modern Spello) is an ancient settlement of Umbria that became a Roman colony in the first century BC.
413171: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.
413172: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.
413174: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.
413175: *Incerulae, an ancient sanctuary site in the territory of the Vestini.
413178: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.
413179: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).
413181: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.
413182: A village of the Marrucini, forming a station on the Via Claudia Valeria between Corfinium and Teate.
413184: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.
413185: Lugnano in Teverina is a comune located in the Province of Terni in the modern Italian region of Umbria. It lies about 60 km south of Perugia and 25 km west of Terni. Archaeological investigation has documented important examples of villa culture as well as Late Antique funereal evidence.
413186: Luni sul Mignone is a site with archaeological evidence for habitation in the later second millennium BC, continuing into the Italian Iron Age. Excavations conducted by the Swedish Institute in Rome (1960-1963) exposed three phases of settlement activity.
413188: Magliano Sabina is located in Lazio, some 50 km north of Rome and some 30 km west of Rieti.
413189: One of two Roman road stations with this name in Italy attested in ancient sources. The Barrington Atlas Directory localizes this one at modern Torrita di Siena.
413192: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.
413194: An ancient harbor of the city of Tarquinia.
413196: Matilica was a municipium in Umbria located near the source of the river Aesis and close to the borders of Picenum. The Liber Coloniarum identifies the settlement as one of the “Civitates Piceni.”
413197: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G3 Matrinum
413200: Mevania (modern Bevagna) was a Roman municipium in Umbria located on the Via Flaminia. The town was enrolled in the tribus Aemilia.
413201: Mevaniola was a Roman city located in the Bidente valley. Its inhabitants were of Umbrian extraction, connected with the settlement of Mevania (Bevagna).
413205: An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.
413206: The tumulus of Montariolo originally measured some 4 meters in height and 50 meters in diameter. It included more than 350 tombs. It was used during several phases, stretching from the ninth to the fifth centuries BCE.
413208: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E1 Montedoro di Scapezzano
413209: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monte S. Angelo
413210: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Monteferetra
413211: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Montefortino
413212: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Montelibretti
413213: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monterano
413216: An Etruscan elite complex of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. located at Poggio Civitate, a hill adjacent to the medieval town of Murlo and about 25 km south of Siena.
413217: Musarna is an ancient Etruscan settlement discovered in 1849 just west of Viterbo, Italy. The École française de Rome has been conducting excavations at the site since 1983.
413223: Shrine dedicated to a rural divinity of the Sabina.
413224: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.
413225: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.
413226: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Novilara
413227: Nuceria (modern Nocera Umbra) is an ancient town in Umbria, perhaps founded in the seventh century B.C. by Camerinum.
413228: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.
413229: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.
413231: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.
413233: [Orcla] or Norchia is an ancient Etruscan settlement located near Tarquinia and along the line of the Roman Via Clodia.
413234: An ancient site in Italy that most likely originates with the Frentani.
413237: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Ostia Aterni
413238: Ostra was an ancient town of Umbria.
413241: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Paganica
413242: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Pallanum
413244: Pliny the Elder discusses the Palmensis Ager in connection with his description of the Praetutii.
413245: Passo Corese is located near Cures (Fara in Sabina). The site is often connected with Titus Tatius' march on Rome in 747 B.C.
413246: Pausulae was a town of Picenum mentioned by Pliny the Elder. It was a Municipium of Regio V.
413247: Peltuinum was a settlement of the Vestini located along the Via Claudia Nova. The town is notable as the birthplace of the Roman general Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo.
413248: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became Colonia Vibia Augusta Perusia quite late, in A.D. 251-3, under Trebonianus Gallus.
413249: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Pescara
413251: A Roman town where the emperor Vespasian was born in A.D. 9.
413252: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Piano Tondo
413254: Pieve di Sant'Antonino a Socana, a Medieval parish church, is built atop the remains of an Etruscan sanctuary.
413255: Pinna (modern Penne) was a center of the Vestini. The site came under Roman control after the Social War (89 BC).
413256: Pisaurum (modern Pésaro) was founded as a Roman colony in the territory of the Picentes in 184 BC.
413258: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Pitigliano
413259: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Pitino
413260: An ancient center of the Vestini.
413261: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pitinum Mergens
413262: An ancient settlement in Umbria, known mostly via its inclusion in the texts of Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy, as well as by means of various epigraphic evidence.
413263: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Planina
413264: Plestia was a municipium of the tribus Ufentina.
413266: Poggio Buco was a pre-Roman site located in the valley of the Fiora River. Its archaeological remains include those of a circuit wall and a necropolis. The archaeological site is located ca. 9 km west of Pitigliano.
413267: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Poggio Sommavilla
413268: An late Roman settlement associated with modern Bomarzo in Italy with nearby Etruscan antecedents.
413269: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Ponte a Buriano
413272: A city settled in an area subjugated by Rome during the fourth century B.C. The local populace rebelled against Rome after the defeat at Cannae (216 B.C.), however the defeat of the Carthaginians eventually led to Potentia's reincorporation into the Roman sphere.
413275: A statio on the road from Nuceria to Ancona.
413276: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Punta La Penna
413278: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Quintianum
413279: Quinto Fiorentino is a place located in the plain of the Arno River to the west of Florence. Its location corresponds to the fifth mile of the Roman road. The site is especially known for two Etruscan tholos-type tombs a thòlos, one of which is the Tomba della Mula, and the other the Tomba della Montagnola.
413281: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Raiano
413282: Rapinium is located on the coast of Etruria between Centumcellae and Graviscae, at modern Bagni Sant'Agostino.
413283: Reate (modern Rieti) was a major Sabine center that came to be captured by Manius Curius Dentatus in late third century B.C.
413284: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Regis Villa/Regae
413285: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Respampani
413288: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.
413293: Saena was an Etruscan city that received a Roman colony (Saena Iulia) in the time of Augustus.
413295: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 S. Anatolia
413296: The village of San Casciano dei Bagni, located south of Siena, Italy, has been frequented since at least the first millennium BCE on account of its thermal springs with supposedly healing properties.
413297: An ancient settlement, architectural complex featuring polygonal masonry, and associated burials at modern S. Erasmo di Cesi dates to the archaic period and has evidence for activity through the third century BCE.
413298: The archaeological remains of an Etruscan settlement were discovered at San Giovenale, close to Blera, Italy, by the Swedish Institute at Rome in the 1950s and 1960s. The ancient name of the site is unknown.
413299: An Etruscan settlement evidenced by its extensive, surviving necropolis, which now lies within the Parco Naturale Regionale Marturanum in the administrative territory of Barbarano Romano, Italy. Its modern name is transferred from a nearby medieval church.
413301: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 S. Pier Maggiore
413303: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 S. Vittore
413306: Sarsina was a town of the Umbri that was captured by Cornelius Scipio in 271 B.C. and was the birthplace of the Latin author Plautus. The necropolis at Sarsina has been extensively studied.
413307: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.
413310: Senonian Gauls founded Sena Gallica at the mouth of the Misa River in the fourth century B.C. This place became the site of Rome's earliest colony on the Adriatic seaboard before 280 B.C. Pompeius Magnus destroyed the city in 82 B.C.
413312: An ancient town in the region of Italy now known as Le Marche, Sentinum is perhaps best known for the pivotal Battle of Sentinum of the Third Samnite War that took place nearby in 295 BC.
413314: Septempeda was an ancient settlement of Picenum. Its Roman phase began as a conciliabulum in the third century B.C.
413315: Sestinum was an ancient place in Umbria near the headwaters of the river Pisaurus. Pliny mentions the site, and its ancient name is preserved in modern toponymy.
413318: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.
413319: Sorrina was a small Etruscan settlement on Viterbo's Colle di San Lorenzo, of which some traces remain. Epigraphic evidence also attests to a Roman municipium - Surrina Nova - that was likely located between Viterbo and Lake Bullicame.
413320: An ancient city along the route of the Via Flaminia; an initial colony was established there in 241 BCE.
413321: Site of an ancient settlement that flourished between the seventh century BCE and the early sixth century CE, located west across the Tiber from the modern village of Attigliano in Italy. Piammiano is probably to be identified with "Statonia", which is mentioned in ancient sources.
413323: Suana (Sovana) has Etruscan origins but later became a Roman municipium. In the fifth century A.D. it became an episcopal see.
413324: Suasa was the site of a Roman municipium in Umbria. It lies in the Piano Volpello along a road from Cales to Sena Gallica. Alaric razed the settlement in 409.
413326: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.
413328: An ancient settlement along the line of what would become the Roman Via Cassia and described by Livy, together with Nepet, as one of the keys to Etruria. A Latin colony was founded at the site after the fall of Veii.
413330: Tadinae (Sant'Antonio della Rasina to the west of Gualdo Tadino) is an ancient municipium of Umbria and was a road station on the Via Flaminia.
413332: An ancient city of Etruria and the leading city of the doudecim populi Etruriae, Tarquinia (called Tarch(u)na or Tarchna in Etruscan) was a major urban center of ancient Italy.
413333: Originally named Teate Marrucinorum, Teate (modern Chieti) was the principal settlement of the Marrucini. Strabo attributes its origins to Arcadian Greeks.
413338: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Tifernum Mataurense
413339: An Umbrian hilltown in the floodplain of the Tiber river north of Perusia.
413342: Tiora Matiene was the site of an ancient oracle of the god Mars. The Barrington Atlas tentatively placed it at modern Teora, near Barete.
413344: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.
413348: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Trea
413349: Trebiae was an ancient city of Umbria (regio IV) located near the line of the Via Flaminia. It is identified with modern Trevi, north of Spoleto in Italy.
413350: Trebula Mutuesca or Trebula Mutusca was one of two Sabine cities bearing the name Trebula.
413352: Trevignano Romano, located on the shores of Lake Bracciano, lies some 47 km from Rome. Archaeological evidence for Etruscan occupation, in the form of tombs dating to the eighth - sixth centuries B.C., has been discovered to the north of the modern town. A medieval castle was built there under Innocent III ca. 1200.
413354: Tuder, modern Todi, is an ancient city of Umbria. Its foundation likely occurred during the eighth/seventh centuries BC, although legendary traditions associate the site with the activities of Herakles.
413355: Tuficum was an ancient city of Umbria located on the Aesis River. It became a municipium of the tribus Oufentina.
413356: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.
413364: An ancient city of Regio V (Picenum) where a Roman colony was founded in the second century B.C.
413365: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Urvinum Hortense
413369: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Vacchereccia
413373: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.
413374: Around the modern Italian town of Verucchio (Emilia-Romagna), a number of ancient necropoleis provide evidence for iron-age civilization and craft at a presumed settlement on the site lasting into the Roman period.
413375: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vespasiae
413377: Vettona (modern Bettona) is an ancient settlement of Umbria located between Perusia and Mevania. Pliny the Elder lists it among the municipalities of Umbria, and it also numbered as one of the “xv Populi Umbriae".
413380: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vicus Martis
413381: Vicus Matrini was a mansio along the Via Cassia, located between Sutri and Forum Cassi. The site's name is attested on the Peutinger Table.
413383: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Vignanello
413384: The remains of a Republican temple podium now support a Christian church at Villa S. Silvestro in Umbria. The temple's podium likely dates, in its first phase, to the third century B.C.
413385: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Villalfonsina
413386: Visentium (Bisenzio) was an Etruscan settlement located on the shores of Lago di Bolsena. The site has yielded especially important evidence for Iron Age and Etruscan period burials.
413387: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Vittorito
413389: Volsinii, also referred to as Volsinii Novi, is thought to be the settlement where Rome resettled the survivors of the Volsinian rebellion of 264 BCE. This episode is discussed by Zonaras (8. 7. 8). A late republican center at Bolsena, Italy, with civic architecture (forum) and domus has been excavated since 1946 by the École Française and is identified as Volsinii Novi.
413393: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.
416806: A shrine of Voltumna that served as the chief religious center of Etruria. The Etruscan League (duodecim populi Etruriae) was said to meet annually at the shrine. Archaeological excavations of the site of Campo della Fiera have been posited as the definitive location of the Fanum Voltumnae.
416834: Referred to by Virgil, Nersa was a vicus of the Aequiculi. Its precise location is not known, but some 19th century scholars identified it with the modern village of Civitella di Nesce in Italy.
416856: A now-unlocated pagus in the territory of the Sabines. Septem Aquae was known for springs and lakes that were popular with tourists. Cicero visited the area in 54 B.C.
422802: A settlement along the Via Laurentina that has yielded significant evidence for protohistoric occupation, including funereal evidence of the eighth and seventh centuries B.C.
422803: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Acquafredda
422811: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Nonum
422821: Aefula was an ancient settlement of Latium that had disappeared by the time of Pliny the Elder, although the cult of Bona Dea there continued to flourish.
422823: Located in the Anio river valley to the south of Subiaco, Afilae was a municipium that was likely assigned to the tribus Aniensis.
422824: Alba Longa, located in the Alban Hills southeast of Rome, was the chief city and founder of the Latin League. Conflict with Rome caused Alba's destruction in the seventh century B.C. The legendary history of Romulus and Remus connects them to the royal lineage of the city. The ancient city is probably to be located at and around the site of modern Castel Gandolfo.
422829: An ancient settlement of Latium located in the territory of the Aequi.
422831: Alsium served as a port for Caere, together with Fregenae. A Roman colony was established ca. 245 BCE. The Antonine Itinerary places it 18 Roman miles from Portus at the mouth of the Tiber.
422832: A small site in Latium (?1.2 hectares) that may have been fortified as early as the eighth century BCE.
422833: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio. By Cicero's time it received the status of municipium.
422835: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Annunziatella
422836: Antemnae is an ancient Latin settlement located north of Rome near the point where the Anio and Tiber rivers intersect. Connected with Rome's early history, Antemnae was involved in episodes such as the 'Rape of the Sabine Women' and Romulus is said to have celebrated a triumph over the Antemnates in 752 BC.
422837: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.
422843: Ardea was an ancient settlement of the Rutuli in Latium.
422844: Aricia was an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.
422845: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Artena
422854: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Buglioncino
422855: Buon Riposo is a small, fortified settlement covering some 2 hectares. Its fortifications date to the seventh century BCE or later.
422857: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cabum?
422859: Caere (also known as Cisra or Cerveteri) was a major Etruscan polis located ca. 50 km north-northwest of Rome in southern Etruria.
422860: A Christian catacomb originally containing the tombs of Pope Callixtus I and Pope Julius I, along with that of the eponymous Saint Calepodius.
422861: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Campo del Fico
422862: Campoverde (Lazio) lies some 60 km south of Rome. In 1977-1978 a quantity of votive material was recovered from a body of water known as the "Laghetto del Monsignore". This spring-fed body of water was interpreted as an open-air votive depository.
422867: The church and convent "I Cappuccini" in Frascati was the site of a Roman villa.
422868: An ancient town on the Via Clodia.
422869: A Roman tomb that supports a Medieval farmhouse (casale) at the sixth mile of the Via Appia. The tomb originally dates ca. 30 BC; it was a large, circular tomb with a diameter of approximately 35 m.
422874: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Casali
422876: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Case Nuove 1
422880: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Castel Campanile
422881: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Le Castella
422882: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Castel Madama
422883: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Castelporziano
422884: Castel Savello takes its name from a fifteenth-century fortress of the Savelli family at Albano Laziale. Funerary evidence associated with the Latial culture has been documented here.
422886: A Latin settlement that became a Roman municipium.
422887: The so-called "Torraccio della Cecchina" is a Roman funereal monument dating to the second century A.D. It is located at the ninth kilometer of the modern Via Nomentana.
422889: The Roman temple dedicated to Ceres and Faustina received patronage from Herodes Atticus. Its remains were eventually repurposed in the construction of the church of Sant'Urbano.
422892: A ruined Roman mausoleum on the grounds of the Caffarella regional park. The so-called Cessati Spiriti mausoleum was once clad in travertine.
422893: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Ciciliano
422894: A major Roman necropolis and catacomb along the Via Nomentana.
422898: Collatia was an ancient city of Latium located between Gabii and the Anio River. A colony of Alba Longa, Collatia was one of the most ancient cities of Latium. Subjugated by Rome under the Tarquins, Collatia would decline during the Republican period and numbers among the lost Latin cities by the accounting of Pliny the Elder.
422899: Colle Gentile is a naturally defensible hill with good visibility located in the environs of Norba. While the site has not been scientifically excavated, it has been surveyed. The Groningen Institute of Archaeology identified traces of polygonal masonry fortification walls as well as surface ceramics that indicate settlement activity associated with Archaic and Republican phases. Imperial period activity is absent.
422901: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Monitola
422904: Colle Rotondo was the site of a prehistoric settlement inhabited from the Bronze Age until the early Iron Age.
422907: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 La Colombella
422909: A Latin center in the Monti Lepini that was already a Roman municipium by 211 B.C.
422910: An ancient town of Latium connected with the origins of Servius Tullius.
422913: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Crepaddosso
422914: An ancient town of Latium located at the headwaters of the Allia river, very close to the territory of the Sabines, Crustumerium figures in Rome's early history. The Romans conquered the site in 500 B.C. and formed the tribus Crustumina or Clustumina in 471 B.C.
422916: The Arval Brethren cultivated the cult of the Dea Dia. The remains of this Augustan era temple, located at La Tavernaccia restaurant in the Magliana Vecchia neighborhood of Rome, are subterranean and not open to the public.
422917: A site sacred to Diana near Lake Nemi, comprised of a Tuscan-style sanctuary and a sacred grove.
422921: An ancient city of Latium that was said to have been conquered by Ancus Marcius, Ficana was located near the eleventh mile of the Via Ostiensis. Excavation at the site has produced important evidence for the urban center beginning from the eighth century BC. Pliny the Elder mentions Ficana as one of the lost cities of Latium.
422922: Ficulea was an ancient city of Latium situated between Rome and Nomentum.
422923: Fidenae was an ancient city of Latium.
422926: A sanctuary dedicated to Fortuna Muliebris along the Via Latina. Tradition holds that it was dedicated in 487 B.C.
422930: An ancient town of Etruria, Fregenae was located between Alsium and the mouth of the river Tiber.
422932: An ancient Latin city located on the line of the Republican Via Praenestina connecting Rome to Praeneste. Gabii is allied to Rome from an early date and flourished during the archaic period, declining by the time of Augustus.
422934: A fourth-century A.D. catacomb along the via Salaria at Rome.
422935: A fortified site on the Via Appia dating to the Republican period.
422941: Grottarossa is located at the intersection of key roadways in northern suburbium of Rome, lying along the Via Flaminia as well as at the point where the Via Veientana separated from the Via Cassia and thereby connected Rome with Veii. There is archaeological evidence for tombs, both built tombs and rock-cut tombs in the exposed tuff escarpments, as well as villas.
422948: An extensive second and third century A.D. necropolis located between the city of Ostia and Portus.
422949: An important Latial sanctuary of Iuppiter located on Mons Albanus (modern Monte Cavo).
422950: A temple located at the fourth mile of the Via Appia.
422952: Originally a member of the Latin League, the city of Labicum was taken by the Romans ca. 418 B.C. By the time of Augustus, the site was almost certainly deserted and its precise location remains debated today.
422956: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battles of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.
422957: A Roman tomb of the second or third century CE.
422960: An ancient city of Latium on the Numicus River that was founded, according to Virgil, by Aeneas.
422968: "Magliana Vecchia" is the name of the 40th urban administrative zone of the Comune di Roma. It is located to the southwest of the city center and straddles the Grande Raccordo Anulare (Ring Road) line that circles the city. The compilers of the Barrington Atlas noted that this place includes a "bridge" and a "settlement". In terms of archaeological remains, numerous sites have been identified in and around Magliana Vecchia, including a Roman bridge and several villas.
422971: The Domus Marmeniae is a villa located on the Via Appia near the fourth milestone. The villa grounds hosted a pagan necropolis and tradition holds that the matrona, Marmenia, relocated the body of St. Urban to a mausoleum built on the grounds.
422973: Monte del Grano is a popular name that was assigned to a mausoleum once thought to belong to Alexander Severus, although that assignation is no longer supported. The archaeological remains are now part of the Parco XVII Aprile 1944.
422974: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Monte dell'Oro
422976: Monteroni, near Ladispoli, is the site of an Etruscan necropolis.
422977: An Etruscan and Roman site lying 4 km to the west of Caere along the monumental road leading to Pyrgi. Until the early 1960s, the site was known for the monumental tumulus that Mengarelli had excavated in the 1920s. Subsequent excavation revealed other evidence, including an elite compound that served as a sanctuary.
422979: Ashby describes the area of the Vigna Montioni as the findspot of numerous funereal inscriptions and funerary altars. This vineyard of the early twentieth century seems likely to have been the location of the villa of the Iavoleni.
422981: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Muraccio dell’Omo
422985: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Nettuno
422986: The Latin town of Nomentum and Rome were linked by means of the Via Nomentana. In Livy's history the town, a member of the Latin League, is captured by Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. Nomentum was one of a number of towns captured by Tarquinius. The Romans granted the town civitas sine suffragio after 338 B.C.
422987: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.
422994: The site of a major Iron Age necropolis (Latial chronology) composed of over 600 burials.
422995: The port city of ancient Rome located at the mouth of the river Tiber.
422997: The Barrington Atlas Directory indicates that an ancient place called Pedum could correspond to the modern Corcolle in Lazio, Italy.
422998: A large Christian basilica discovered in 1976 several hundred meters southeast of the Porta Laurentina of Ostia. The original phase dates to the end of the fourth century A.D.
423005: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Pometia
423006: A villa attributed to Cnaeus Pompeius at Albano Laziale.
423010: Ponte Mammolo is the modern name of an ancient bridge over the Aniene river. It gives its name to a neighborhood and metro station in the northeast part of the modern city of Rome. Archaeological evidence of ancient quarrying and a settlement have also been found in the vicinity of the bridge.
423012: The great ancient maritime port of Rome, located on the right-hand bank of the Tiber River.
423013: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla founded a new colony there in the first century B.C.
423015: Prima Porta, located to the north of Rome, allegedly derives its modern name from the remains of a Roman aqueduct whose presence signaled to travelers on the Via Flaminia that they had reached Rome. The site is best known for an Imperial villa that belonged to the family of Livia Drusilla.
423016: A Christian catacomb within an ancient quarry on the Via Salaria that was in use from the second to the fourth centuries AD. The Catacomb of Priscilla was likely named for Priscilla, a member of the gens Acilia, and contains the oldest known Marian painting (third century AD).
423022: The Tomb of Annia Regilla (vix. A.D. 125-160), the wife of Herodes Atticus. The tomb is also erroneously known as the "Temple of the God Rediculum" and was used in the Middle Ages as a hay barn.
423024: The sanctuary of the god Robigus, located at the sixth mile of the Via Cassia. The Romans celebrated the festival of Robigalia on 25 April.
423026: La Rustica was a Latin site located along the Via Collatina.
423029: Sacer Mons is a hill on the banks of the Anio River and is connected, traditionally, with the episode of the secession of the Roman plebs of 494 BC.
423030: The Monastery of Saint Benedict or Monastero di San Benedetto Sacro Speco. The Shrine of the Sacred Cave of St. Benedict (Sacro Speco di San Benedetto) at Subiaco is a significant monastic shrine connected to the Roman Catholic saint Benedict. At the site is found a fresco-adorned cave linked to the saint, dating to the eighth century.
423033: S. Agapito, the Palestrina Cathedral also known as the Cattedrale di Sant'Agapito martire, was built atop the ruins of Praeneste's civic forum and its temple. The relics of Saint Agapitus were transferred to this location in 898. The present basilica was consecrated on 16 December 1117 by Pope Pasquale I.
423034: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Agata
423035: A titular church on the Via Nomentana, S. Agnese houses the remains of the eponymous saint. The present church was built by Pope Honorius I in the seventh century AD, on the site of a fourth century basilica built by Constantine I.
423036: The basilica and catacombs of S. Alessandro are located at the seventh milestone of the Via Nomentana.
423038: A large catacomb on the Via Appia south of Rome notable especially for its so-called 'Crypt of the Popes'. The catacomb covers approximately 15 hectares.
423041: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E2 S. Clemens
423042: S. Ermete is the site of a Paleochristian basilica and catacomb; the catacombs are also referred to as the Catacombs of Bassilla, and both names occur in the documentary sources.
423043: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Felicita
423045: A catacomb connected with the Christian Saint Hippolytus of Rome along the Via Tiburtina.
423046: The Papal Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls (Basilica Papale di San Lorenzo fuori le Mura) is one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome. The basilica serves as the shrine and tomb dedicated to Saint Lawrence and its earliest phases likely belong to the fourth century AD.
423047: The so-called "Archi di San Lidano" are the remains of a Roman stone bridge in the Pontine plain, near the modern locality of Sezze Scalo. The bridge likely dates originally to the second century B.C. Evidence of an ancient sanctuary have also been detected in the vicinity.
423048: The church of Saints Marcellinus and Peter is a Roman Catholic church located on the Via Merulana in Rome. Pope Siricius built the original church in the fourth century A.D., close to the catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter. The relics of the saints were deposited in the church in 1256.
423049: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B1 S. Maria di Galeria
423051: S. Passera is a Christian church on the Tiber river in Rome, opposite the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls. The current church dates to the ninth century and incorporated the remains of a Roman tomb. The church is traditionally connected to a community of local miners.
423052: One of Rome's four major papal basilicae, S. Paulus was founded by Constantine I in the early fourth century A.D. and expanded by Valentinian I in the 370s. The basilica, with many renovations, repairs, and improvements, stood until the 19th century, when it was destroyed in a fire. The reconstructed basilica only generally resembles the original structure.
423053: The Basilica of St. Peter in Vatican City is currently a Renaissance edifice standing on the site of Old St. Peter's Basilica, a church built by Constantine I between 319 and 333 CE. The holy site is located on the Mons Vaticanus in connection with the purported site of the burial of the Christian Saint Peter.
423054: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Rufina
423055: A convent founded within the area of the Villa Neronis.
423056: S. Sebastianus (San Sebastiano fuori le mura) is a Christian basilica outside the walls of Rome; the earliest phase belongs to the fourth century AD.
423057: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Sinforosa
423058: A Christian catacomb along the Via Flaminia dedicated to S. Valentino.
423059: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D1 S. Vincenzo
423060: An ancient settlement on the right bank of the river Astura, Satricum has a mixed heritage of Latins and Volscians. In 499 B.C. Satricum was a member of the Latin League, but was under Volscian control in 488 B.C. The site is noted for its sanctuary of Mater Matuta.
423063: The tomb C. Maenius Bassus is located along the Via Valeria. This podium tomb with superstructure is dated to either the reign of Caius or that of Claudius. Epigraphic evidence mentions that C. Maenius C. f. Cam. Bassus was an Augustalis, an aedile, and praefectus fabrum.
423064: A tomb on the Via Appia south of Rome belonging to Caecilia Metella, a daughter of Metellus Creticus. She was born ca. 100 BC. In 1303, the tomb was incorporated into the Castrum Caetani, serving as the main tower of the fortification.
423065: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that is traditionally believed to be that of Publius Septimius Geta, the younger son of Septimius Severus.
423066: The Mausoleum of the Plautii dates to the first century B.C. It is located near Ponte Lucano at Tibur.
423067: The small hill that is known as "Il Poggio di Serrone di Bove" is located in the hinterland of ancient Norba and was the site of ancient settlement activity. Architectural remains on the site include those of a polygonal masonry sub-struction or platform as well as an ancient roadway that may be part of the road tract from Norba to Cora.
423068: A Volscian settlement of the fifth century B.C. that became a Latin colony in 382 B.C.
423071: An archaeological site located at the midpoint of the Via Tiburtina linking Rome and Tibur.
423072: A city of Latium Adjectum established as a Latin colony ca. 494 B.C.
423076: A station on the Via Cassia attested in an inscription dated to A.D. 379-383.
423078: An ancient settlement, located at modern Subiaco in Italy, Sublaqueum was located in the territory of the Aequi that was annexed by Rome in 304 B.C.
423081: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.
423083: A Roman tomb near Albano Laziale connected in tradition with the story of the contest between the Horatii and Curiatii.
423084: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tomba di Marco Plauzio Lucano
423085: An imperial Roman tomb of Publius Vibius Marianus, erroneously identified as the Tomba di Nerone (Tomb of Nero) by G. B. Piranesi.
423087: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tor Angela
423089: The modern toponym Tor Marancia is claimed to derive from the Praedium Amaranthianus, a villa belonging to the second-century A.D. freedman Amaranthus.
423091: A Roman tomb, known as the Torraccia dell’Inviolata. This tomb has a cruciform plan that is inscribed within a circular structure. Based on masonry techniques the tomb dates to the later first or second century.
423092: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Il Torraccio
423093: A circular mausoleum dating to the Late Republican period along the Via Praenestina.
423094: The so-called "Il Torraccio (1)" is the cement core of a Roman tomb located at the twelfth milestone of the Via Appia Nuova, on the left side.
423096: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Torre del Monumento
423097: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Torre del Padiglione
423099: A Final Bronze Age settlement of four to five hectares in South Etruria.
423101: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Torre Sessano
423102: An Iron Age settlement in Latium.
423104: A Latin federal sanctuary at Lavinium, consisting of a series of altars that range in date from the sixth to the second century BC and a sacred site (or heroon) connected with the hero Aeneas.
423106: A statio at the point where the Via Appia crosses the Via Ninfina.
423107: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Troia?
423108: Tusculum was a Latin city of the Alban Hills in central Italy. After 381 B.C., Tusculum became the first "municipium cum suffragio".
423114: An Iron Age settlement and necropolis located in the Monti Lepini near the abbey of Valvisciolo, characterized by polygonal masonry terrace walls. While the ancient name of the site is unknown, various proposals have been raised, including Sulmo (Savignoni, Mengarelli) and Pometia (Ogilvie). The settlement corresponds to the Latial II B phase and occupation ends ca. the late sixth century B.C.
423115: Varia (modern Vicovaro) was a settlement of the Sabines.
423116: An important city of South Etruria located north-northwest of Rome, Veii was eventually sacked by the Romans in 396 B.C. The ancient city covered some 180 ha.
423117: Velitrae (modern Velletri) was an ancient Volscian settlement. In the Roman Republican period, Velitrae was attacked by Marcus Furius Camillus (379 B.C.) and again by Cincinnatus (377 B.C.); the Romans controlled the site by 365 B.C. The gens Octavia hailed from the city and a youthful Octavian spent time there.
437043462: The church of San Paolo at Peltuinum likely dates to the seventh or eighth century CE.
482028558: The small Aegean island of Tsimintiri, located between Despotiko and Antiparos, has produced archaeological evidence for a large sanctuary and/or other public complex of archaic date, likely to be associated with the extensive archaic sanctuary of Mandra, located on the island of Despotiko, to which Tsimintiri was connected in antiquity.
780954288: A tetrastyle temple in the Corinthian order sacred to Zeus Megistos was built at Canatha by the first century CE.
807514119: The marketplace of the ancient city of Athens in Greece.
219478548: A monumental altar built around the third century B.C. that was probably dedicated to Zeus Eleutherios. Remains of the altar are located in the archaeological area of Neapolis in Syracuse, Sicily.
715252914: A Catholic sanctuary on Mount Gargano, in northern Apulia, Italy. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.
59677979: A Longobard church in Benevento, Italy, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.
459393126: An ancient Elamite complex founded ca. 1250 BC by the king Untash-Napirisha. Tchogha Zanbil was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.
578501279: A segment of an imperial necropolis preserved along a portion of a consular road on the Vatican Hill. The Via Triumphalis necropolis was uncovered during the construction of a parking structure in the Via del Pellegrino.
292134118: A Chalcolithic to Bronze Age settlement mounded identified in 1989, located on the east bank of the Euphrates River, 75 km southwest of Şanlıurfa. The mound measures ca. 15 meters high and 70 x 60 meters in area.
979582397: An ancient settlement mound located 45 kilometers north of Şanlıurfa, Turkey, Titris Hoyuk lies near the Euphrates River valley. There were several phases of occupation in the third and second millennia BCE.
222740561: The ancient monument referred to as "Trajan's Kiosk" or the "Pharaoh's Bed" is an incomplete hypaethral temple that dates to the second century CE. The monument is currently located on Agilkia Island although it was originally built on the island of Philae. It was relocated in the 1960s as part of the International Campaign to Save the Monuments of Nubia.
651950411: An extensive necropolis of the Kerma culture located on Sai Island.
466639527: The remains of an ancient village, perhaps linked to ancient Berenice Troglodytica.
204558111: The Temple of Apedemak, also known as the Lion Temple, is located to the west of the temple of Amun.
572048102: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is generally identified with Tell Fekheriye (Tell Faḫārīya).
135544311: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that has been identified with Tell Tūrin and Thiltauri of the Tabula Pentingeriana.
427224440: This place was published as an unintended duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/814675/.
957515415: An archaeological site in northeastern Syria inhabited in the Early Dynastic through post-Akkadian period (ca. 2750-1800 BCE).
420811320: Site on the Red Sea Coast in Egypt, used in the Fourth Dynasty as a port for importing turquoise and copper from Sinai. The oldest surviving papyrus from Egypt, dated during the reign of Khufu (26th century BCE), was found at the site.
560130183: Walled citadel in Carthage built in the early first millennium BCE. The site was destroyed during the Third Punic War in 146 BCE by the forces of Scipio Aemilianus. The hill became the site of the city's forum in the Roman period.
48167301: Temple 1, also referred to as the "Great Temple", is located in the lower city of Hattusa. It dates to the thirteenth century B.C.
584305092: Near a bath complex built under Commodus, a Severan complex that included a plaza, porticoes, and a temple dedicated to the Severan family was added.
122572945: A sanctuary of Apollo Lyceios in Athens, which served as the seat of Aristotle's Peripatetic school of philosophy founded in 335/4 BCE. The Lyceum was destroyed by Sulla in 86 BCE.
383321670: The Roman temple of Vic dates to the second century A.D.
236385: The Citânia de Briteiros is an archaeological site of the Castro culture located in the northwestern part of the Iberian Peninsula.
236387: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 H4 Brittablo
236392: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 E3 Cabeza de S. Pedro
236395: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 D3 Caladunum
236396: Cale was the site of an ancient city located at the mouth of the Durius fl. The Roman colony Portus Cale was established there in 136 BC.
236397: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 D3 Caliabriga/Calabria
236405: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 E4 Capera
236409: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 24 D3 Cárquere

893987: Dilbat (modern Tell ed-Duleym), a small city southeast of Babylon on the eastern bank of the Euphrates River, was the cult center of the god Uraš and the goddess Ninegal. The site consists of two mounds of ruins: the larger, eastern mound contains the remains of earlier building phases (going back to the city’s founding in the Early Dynastic Period, ca. 2700 BC), while the smaller, western ruin hill contains the first-millennium-BC and later building occupations (down to the early Islamic Period). Little is known about the cultic topography of this small Babylonian city. Two first-millennium-BC ziggurat lists and a few Neo-Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian royal inscriptions record that Dilbat’s main temple was E-ibbi-Anum and its ziggurat was Eguba’anki, both were dedicated to Uraš. The temple of Ninegal (Bēlet-ēkalli) might have been named Esapar. Recent excavations on the eastern mound have unearthed the Kassite-Period remains of E-ibbi-Anum.

894019: In the ninth century BC, Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883-859 BC) built himself a new administrative center.
